mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 3.0% (historical threshold).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate above 4.8% signals economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.8%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and industrial production indicate a broad-based economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced business investment and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and INDPRO fails to predict negative returns: 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%), the Federal Reserve typically tightens monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as higher rates pressure equity valuations.
failure_condition: In periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) reflect strong consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings prospects improve.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 110.0 signals manufacturing sector weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth fears intensify.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 110.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an overheating economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated monetary tightening.
failure_condition: The joint increase in PAYEMS and stable FEDFUNDS fails to predict negative returns: 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized) signals robust economic expansion, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits rise and investor confidence strengthens.
failure_condition: In periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% annualized, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.
